structure: Part 7, Transporter. Read in full at commit 04a073b (the checkout's HEAD): the four DR2.1 views app/views/design-release-2.1/transporter.html (183 lines), transporter-add.html (95), transporter-add-private.html (63) and transporter-add-commercial.html (67); the root partials app/views/partials/transporter-add-private-fields.html (112), transporter-add-commercial-fields.html (236) and transporter-authorisation-banner.html (21); app/data/transporters.js (8 seeded transporters) and app/data/transporter-types.js (2 types); app/routes.js lines 3289-3842 (transporter search and results, the transporter page render, session sync, type validation, the private and commercial form defaults, parsing, validation, object builders, success message, address-book mapping, save and cancel redirect, and the private and commercial render functions) and lines 12664-12858 (GET /transport-details, GET /transporter, GET and POST /transporter/add, GET and POST /transporter/add/private, GET and POST /transporter/add/commercial, POST /transporter). Also glanced, for context only and not claimed beyond what these pages show: partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html (the transporter page's buttons) and routes.js buildAddressBookCountryItems at line 10412 (the private country list). Pages covered: Transporter details (/transporter, reached also by /transport-details), Choose a transporter type (/transporter/add), Add a private transporter (/transporter/add/private) and Add a commercial transporter (/transporter/add/commercial), each under /design-release-2.1 through the version mount. Claims follow page order: the transporter page (caption, heading, intro, authorisation guidance, search, add button, results table and its eight seeded rows, selection, buttons, what is saved and where it goes), then the type page, then the private form, then the commercial form (including the DR2.1 address lookup), then save, success message, cancel, and the address-book entry made when the add flow starts from the address book. The transporter page has no validation of its own: a missing selection continues without an error, recorded as an inferred claim and a gap.

claims.statement: The transporter page can show a transporter-selection error message above the table, but no handler sets one: posting the page with no transporter selected continues to the next journey page without an error.
claims.note: The template checks data.errors.transporterId, but nothing in routes.js lines 12664-12858 or 3289-3842 sets it. Transporter selection is therefore optional on this page.

claims.statement: The prototype gives no wording for an error when no transporter is selected on the transporter page.
claims.note: Looked in the transporter view and POST /transporter handler; the error slot exists with no message defined anywhere in this slice.

claims.statement: Continuing from the transporter page with a transporter selected saves the selected transporter's id, name, address, approval number, type and status to the notification.
claims.quote:
sessionData.transporterId = transporter.id
  sessionData.transporter = {
    name: transporter.name,
    address: transporter.address,
    approvalNumber: transporter.approvalNumber,
    type: transporter.type,
    status: transporter.status
  }

claims.statement: After saving, the transporter page continues to the next page in the journey after /transporter (or the section's continue destination).

Using a soft-save action on the transporter page (such as 'Save and return to overview') saves the selected transporter if one is chosen and returns to the notification hub (or the save destination for that action).
The transporter details step counts as complete when a transporter with a name has been saved.
By default the transporter page shows a 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification hub.
claims.note: The shared journey-form-actions partial is the shell part's; claimed here only for what the transporter page shows.

claims.statement: When the notification is being amended, the transporter page shows 'Save and return' (to review), a secondary 'Save and continue', and a 'Save and return to overview' link-style button.
When the transporter page is edited from a template review, it shows a single 'Save and return' button and a 'Cancel' link back to the template.
After a new transporter is added from the journey, the transporter page shows a one-time 'Success' notification banner with the success message, which is cleared once shown.

The success message is '<name> transporter added', where the transporter name is shown with only its first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased (so 'ACME Haulage' shows as 'Acme haulage transporter added').
claims.note: The lower-casing of the rest of the name looks unintentional (it mangles proper nouns and 'Ltd'); recorded as the prototype does it.

claims.statement: If the new transporter has no name, the success message is 'Transporter added'.

Choosing 'Commercial' saves the chosen type and goes to the add commercial transporter page (/transporter/add/commercial).

claims.statement: The prototype has no format validation messages for the transporter email address, phone number or postcode.
claims.note: Both validators check only that each required field is present. Looked in validateTransporterPrivateForm and validateTransporterCommercialForm.

claims.statement: All private and commercial transporter inputs are trimmed of surrounding whitespace before validation and saving.
When the private or commercial form has errors, the page is shown again with every error listed in field order in the summary and beside each field, and the entered values kept.
Values entered on an invalid private or commercial form are kept in the session and shown again if the user later returns to that page, until the form is saved or cancelled.
claims.note: Inferred: the form defaults read the stored form, which is cleared only on success or cancel.

claims.statement: Both add pages have a primary 'Save and continue' button.

claims.note: From the journey, cancel goes to the dashboard rather than back to the transporter page.

claims.statement: The commercial transporter form posts to /design-release-2.1/transporter/add/commercial and shows a 'There is a problem' error summary when it has errors.

Commercial transporter field 'Transporter authorisation number' (transporterCommercialAuthorisationNumber) is first on the form and required; when blank the error is 'Enter a transporter authorisation number'. Its format is not checked.

claims.statement: Under DR2.1 the commercial transporter page offers an address search labelled 'Search for an address' with the placeholder 'Start typing...', which searches the Northern Ireland lookup addresses.
claims.note: showAddressLookup is true when isDesignRelease2Version is set, which DR2.1 also sets. The lookup address list itself lives in an address-book data file outside this slice.

claims.statement: The address search results are announced as 'Address search results' and the search button has the accessible name 'Search'.
Choosing a looked-up address fills the commercial transporter's name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode from that address wherever the user left the field blank.
The commercial transporter page has an 'Enter address manually' link-style button that reveals the manual address fields.

With the address lookup on, the manual address fields and the contact details section start hidden, and are shown when an address has been looked up, when address line 1 already has a value, when an address field has an error, or after any failed save.
claims.quote:
const showManualAddress = locals.showManualAddress != null
    ? locals.showManualAddress
    : (
      !showAddressLookup ||
      hasAddressErrors ||
      Boolean(locals.selectedLookupAddressId) ||
      Boolean(formValues.addressLine1)
    )
claims.note: The contact details section is also revealed client-side once an address is chosen (data-reveal-with-address).

claims.statement: The address search field can show an address lookup error, but no handler sets one, so the prototype defines no wording for it.
claims.note: validateTransporterCommercialForm never adds an addressLookup error; looked in routes.js 3289-3842 and 12664-12858.

claims.statement: Commercial transporter field 'Address line 1' (transporterCommercialAddressLine1) is required; when blank the error is 'Enter address line 1'.
Commercial transporter field 'Address line 2 (optional)' (transporterCommercialAddressLine2) is optional and has no validation.
Commercial transporter field 'Town or city' (transporterCommercialTownOrCity) is required; when blank the error is 'Enter a town or city'.
Commercial transporter field 'County (optional)' (transporterCommercialCounty) is optional and has no validation.
Commercial transporter field 'Postcode or Zip code' (transporterCommercialPostcode) is required; when blank the error is 'Enter a postcode or Zip code'.

A commercial transporter's country is always Northern Ireland: the 'Country' dropdown shows only Northern Ireland and is disabled, a hidden field sends the value, and the server sets it regardless of what is posted.
The commercial validator has a 'Select a country' error for a missing country, which cannot fire because the country is always set to Northern Ireland.
claims.note: Inferred from parseTransporterCommercialFormBody always setting country to COMMERCIAL_TRANSPORTER_COUNTRY.

claims.statement: The commercial transporter form has an 'Enter contact details' section with 'Email address' (required, error 'Enter an email address') and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code', required, error 'Enter a phone number').

A saved commercial transporter is recorded with type Commercial, status New, the entered authorisation number as its approval number, and an address joined from its address lines, town, county, postcode and Northern Ireland.
Saving a new private or commercial transporter adds it to the top of the session's transporter list and makes it the notification's selected transporter.
When the add was started from the journey, saving returns to the transporter page with the success banner, and the new transporter is not added to the address book.
claims.note: Inferred: only the fromAddressBook branch writes to addressBookAddedAddresses. A transporter added in the journey appears in the transporter list only, not as an address-book entry.

claims.statement: When the add was started from the address book, saving adds the new transporter to the address book as a transporter entry (with its type label Private or Commercial, address, approval number, country, and contact details) at the top of the list.

When the add was started from the address book, saving shows the address book's success message, clears the address-book flag and the chosen type, and goes to the address book filtered to transporters.
